messages:
incident-bot: P1 alert: Dedicated pool 'resv-west-1' reached 100% reserved GPU utilization. Queue length spiked to 18k, avg wait 42s. Paging oncall. link: https://internal.redwood/incident/2470012345 :rotating_light:

pagerduty: Paging maya (oncall-sre). escalation policy: dedicated-capacity.

maya: I'm on it. starting triage — pulling metrics, autoscaler logs.

ashok: I'm nearby, can look at autoscale controller. if this is an eviction loop, we'll need to throttle tenants.

ben: tagging infra/alloc team. AcmeCorp reserved block looks saturated. any noisy-tenant flags?

maya: Quick checks: reserved utilization 100% across 4 nodes. autoscaler saw sustained pending pods >1000 for 12m. controller error: "scaleLimitReached" in logs.

maya: commands I'm running:
```
# check autoscaler events
kubectl -n resv-system logs deploy/autoscaler --since=15m | tail -n 200
# list tenants with pending queue
redwood adm pending-queues --pool resv-west-1 --top 20
```

ashok: paste from autoscaler: `E0501 10:23:45 scale.go:128] cannot scale: reached hard capacity limit for pool resv-west-1 (limit=64 GPUs)`

ben: ah, capacity hard cap hit. that's why scaleLimitReached. Did reservation burst policy allow temporary burst?

maya: Burst config shows max_burst=12 but pool already allocated to reserved commitments; no spare GPUs in region.

joel: Oncall note: noisy tenant detection fired for tenant-omega. They have long-running heavy streams that bypass batching. I can run an emergency eviction if we agree.

elena: CS -> affected customers thread: AcmeCorp and NovaHealth have increased 5xx and long tail latency. I'll start notification draft but need exact impact numbers.

maya: agreed, propose this triage path: 1) enable per-tenant soft throttles for heavy tenants 2) attempt emergency preemption of long-running jobs from noisy tenants 3) route new requests to compatible small-LLM variant where possible 4) request short-term capacity bump from cloud team (if available)

ashok: I can push throttles now. running: `redwood adm throttle --pool resv-west-1 --tenant tenant-omega --qps 2 --duration 15m`

joel: Doing eviction probe: `kubectl -n resv-workloads delete pod -l tenant=tenant-omega --grace-period=10` (will cause job restarts, but frees hosts).

incident-bot: action taken: tenant-omega throttled, 15m window. eviction probe started.

maya: after throttle started, pending queue dropped from 18k -> 9.2k in ~3m. latency improved slightly. good signal.

ashok: autoscaler still blocked by hard capacity limit; cloud team ticket created: CT-9423 requesting +8 GPUs for resv-west-1. pinging infra-runner.

ben: meanwhile can we fallback some routes? config snippet to route non-critical customers to hosted pool:
```
route.overrides: |
  - match: tenant in (dev-*, test-*)
    target: hosted-lowcost
  - match: model in (gpt-small-v1)
    target: hosted-lowcost
```

elena: Sent initial customer note: "We are experiencing elevated inference latency in West region; our engineers are actively mitigating. Next update in 15m." cc: AcmeCorp-SRE, NovaHealth-ops.

cs-bot: Customer impact list updated. affected_customers: ["AcmeCorp","NovaHealth","GreenfieldPay"], estimated_impact_window: "~20m", severity: "P1".

maya: telemetry now shows drop to 6.1k pending after eviction actions and throttles. CPU/GPU reclaim on nodes freed ~10% usable memory but GPUs still at 100%.

ashok: cloud squad responded: can add 4 GPUs in 6m, but need approval for budget / spot vs on-demand. Request accepted for +4 GPUs immediate (spot).

ben: Good interim. Also rolling out a model-variant fallback for high-latency routes. deploy snippet:
```
# quick flag
redwood feature-flag set route-fallback-resv-west1 true --ttl 30m
```

maya: After +4 GPUs and continued throttles, queue at 2.3k, avg wait 9s. but some enterprise reserved sessions still hitting timeouts — NovaHealth reports failed batches for >30s.

elena: NovaHealth response: their ingestion retries spiked; they've queued some client-side backoff. CS recommends higher visibility for the next hour.

joel: Note: eviction of tenant-omega caused two long jobs to restart; we saw a transient 502 surge for their requests. cleanup scripts running to reconcile state.

incident-bot: metric checkpoint: 10:40 UTC: pending=2300, avg_wait=9s, reserved_util=96%, throttled_tenants=1. logged in incident at https://internal.redwood/incident/2470012345/logs

maya: I'll keep monitoring autoscaler logs. next steps: 1) confirm cloud can add further capacity if queue rises 2) follow up with tenant-omega ownership for long-term mitigation 3) schedule retro + quotas review.

ashok: I'll open a follow-up CR to add a soft-overcommit buffer so reserved pools can borrow small amount for short bursts. ticket INFRA-1189.

ben: Also let's add a canary test to detect streaming-heavy workloads that bypass batching — we need earlier detection.

elena: Customer update sent: "Mitigations in place; we expect restored performance within 30 minutes. We will follow up with post-incident details."

maya: closing active mitigations; will remain in thread for 30m watch. if queue rises >3k re-escalate.

cs-bot: Noted for follow-up: outreach owners for AcmeCorp and NovaHealth assigned to elena.

joel: quick postmortem bullets (for when we doc): root cause: reserved pool hard capacity + noisy tenant streaming jobs bypassing batching + autoscaler limit. mitigations: throttles + eviction + short capacity bump + route fallbacks. action items: INFRA-1189, SRE-1190 (noisy-tenant detection), CS-224 (customer comms).

elena: Thanks team. I'll close the customer-facing incident note once metrics stable for 30m. :white_check_mark:
